summary: @servicetitan/testing-library 6.6.6 preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a preinstall lifecycle hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts the platform-specific `bun`/`bun.exe` binary, marks it executable, and invokes it against a bundled sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~728 KB heavily obfuscated Bun-compiled script (marked `// @bun @bun-cjs`, containing a rotated opcode/string array and a shuffling function `WV8StW` with hex-named identifiers). The obfuscated payload is not referenced by anything in `dist/` and is not part of the advertised React testing-library API — it exists solely to be run under the freshly dropped Bun runtime at install time. The runtime-swap causes fully arbitrary code execution on the installer at `npm install` time while bypassing Node-based static analysis of the payload. Package metadata is inconsistent with a legitimate ServiceTitan release: empty `description`, a `6.6.6` version, and a preinstall dropper not present in the maintainer's normal publish flow — consistent with a scope hijack or compromised-account release rather than a genuine @servicetitan artifact.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
